The outward «radiation/thermal» pressure/force is balanced by the «inward» gravitational pressure/force ✓
Need to see reference to gravitational force/pressure. Do not accept “gravity”.

The core of star A is at a much higher temperature than the surface ✓

question.html:
Star A is a main sequence star.

The data for Star A and the Sun are given in a table.


a.i State how physical stability is maintained in main sequence stars. [1]

a.ii Explain why nuclear fusion in the core of the star occurs when the temperature and density exceed threshold values. [2]

a.iii Outline why regions of convection form in Star A. [2]

b.i Calculate, in m, the distance to Star A from Earth. [1]

b.ii Show that the luminosity of Star A is about half that of the Sun. [1]

b.iii Deduce the apparent brightness of Star A compared to the apparent brightness of the Sun. [3]

c.i Show that the peak wavelength emitted from Star A is about 560 nm. [1]

c.ii Calculate the energy of a photon of light emitted at this peak wavelength. [2]

c.iii

The peak wavelength of the radiation from Star A is measured by an observer on Earth. The observed wavelength is 0.007% less than the value in (c)(i).

Outline how this difference arises.

[2]

c.iv Determine the speed, in km s–1, of Star A relative to Earth. [2]

d Describe how the light from stars is studied to determine their composition. [3]
